title.title: Finite Smith–Toda complexes at every height
title.subtitle: Claim: for every $n$ there is a prime $p$ and a finite spectrum $V(n)$ killing $p, v_1, \ldots, v_n$ once

plain: Stable shapes are built from basic 'atoms' in layers; atoms in layer four and above were not known to exist

object.heading: $BP_*V(n) = BP_*/(p, v_1, \ldots, v_n)$, all exponents one
object.caption: grey: known for large enough $p$ · colour: claimed, at a prime depending on $n$

beats.text: The Moore spectrum $V(0)$, then $V(1)$ to $V(3)$ for $p > 2, 4, 6$
Whether $V(4)$ exists at any prime was open. The claim: every $V(n)$ exists
Built in an ultraproduct over primes, then descended to one large $p$

steps: Look at all primes at once, in a so-called ultraproduct
There the obstructions become pure algebra, and the tower is built
Only finitely many maps are needed, so they come down to one big prime

achievement.label: Smith–Toda complexes at every height (V(4) open at every prime)
statement: \forall n\ \exists p:\ BP_*V(n) = BP_*/(p, v_1, \ldots, v_n)
achievement.context: Consistent with Nave: $V((p+1)/2)$ never exists for $p \ge 7$, and here $p$ grows with $n$
achievement.note: The prime is not explicit, except a separate $V(4)$ at $p = 1009$

verify.detail: Manuscript only; the explicit $V(4)$ at $p = 1009$ is a separate 44-page paper
verify.ourCheck: We read the construction's outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Each complex kills one more layer. Whether V four exists anywhere was open.
Work across all primes at once, then come down to one large prime.
Claimed: every height, at some prime.

sources.quote: Smith-Toda: V(0) Moore spectrum; V(1),V(2),V(3) exist for p > 2,4,6 (Adams, Smith, Toda). Nave (Annals 2010): V((p+1)/2) does not exist for p >= 7.
The explicit p=1009 V(4) paper is a separate 44-page construction I did not check.
